analysis: The PR adds a typed MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngineError.missingUserQuery. Qwen35TemplateFix.validateUserQuery (Qwen35TemplateFixes.swift:52-63) is called from ChatTemplateFixes.normalizeMessages (ChatTemplateFixes.swift:38). It rejects Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 and Bonsai 2 histories whose only user turns are <tool_response> wrappers, so the failure is a 400 client error instead of a template-raise 500. ProviderLoop+ErrorMapping.swift maps the new case to reason .clientError, failure code .invalidRequest and status 400, in the same way as .invalidToolPayload. The error description is a static string, so no prompt content is echoed on the provider-to-coordinator wire (relevant to A-001, TB-002). I found no new trust-boundary, crypto, attestation or cache surface. The change touches nothing in T-041's SSD cache files, key handling or attestation paths. The only prompt-derived input is user text, which is inspected locally and never serialized. Observations that do not rise to findings: (1) the validator matches context.modelType exactly, without the trim and lowercase that applies(to:) uses, so a differently-cased model_type skips the check and gets the old template-raise 500 (a non-security fallback). (2) It only inspects String content, so a user message with content parts counts as a valid query, which fails safe. (3) The validator is skipped on the MiMo early-return path and the typed OpenAIChatMessage multimodal path, which are unchanged. (4) Other exhaustive switches over this enum in unretrieved files may need the new case; that would be a compile-time concern. This is a 400 path that stops a client-triggerable 500 from counting against provider reputation. Callers outside the supplied batch were not examined, so the coordinator's handling of the 400 was not reviewed.
